results.reason: Creating a mesh and offline 3D preview from a GarmentCode sewing-pattern JSON is directly covered, even without physics.
CPU draping of a GarmentCodeData sample with its body and measurements, plus GLB and run records, is the described simulation workflow.
The description covers previews of existing GarmentCodeData PLY garments; missing patterns and a request to avoid recomputation do not remove that applicability.
A draped garment demo using a real GarmentCode example without a supplied sample is explicitly within the described scope.
Explaining and implementing the GarmentCode pattern-to-stitching-to-XPBD pipeline, including commands and body prerequisites, is directly covered.
An implausible early-static result in GarmentCode CPU simulation and regeneration of its preview match the described troubleshooting scope.
Interpreting GarmentCode simulation quality claims and exporting a viewer that accurately describes the result are covered by quality reporting and preview work.
Determining whether the requested person's GarmentCode simulation can run with a missing body mesh is a pipeline prerequisite and troubleshooting task.
Converting an existing GarmentCode garment OBJ to correctly scaled GLB and an offline preview falls within existing garment preview support.
Remeshing an edited GarmentCode pattern and rerunning CPU draping with initial and final artifacts is a direct use of the described workflow.
This is a generic mechanical-model viewer and export task, explicitly outside garment meshing or draping.
A two-particle mathematical explanation of PBD and XPBD is a generic physics lesson, which the description excludes.
The deliverable is React page layout around an existing video; the button text does not introduce garment geometry or a simulation workflow.
Editing seam allowance in SVG and exporting DXF remains a 2D CAD task, explicitly excluded by the description.
The user requests Blender-only collision correction and baking while retaining that project, which the description excludes.
Debugging NaNs in a mechanical point-cloud export is generic geometry code unrelated to the described garment pipeline.
Translating the paper introduction without implementation analysis is paper translation, an explicit exclusion.
Aggregating metadata and charting counts is dataset statistics, with no garment geometry or simulation work; that is explicitly excluded.
Changing only an existing site's custom domain is deployment-only work, explicitly excluded regardless of the site's name.
Repairing evaluation JSON aggregation and unit tests is ordinary tooling maintenance, with no need for the garment meshing or draping workflow.
